freetrade.guide.header: Formula: %s · Sell tax: %s · Buy tax: %s · Treasury: %s
freetrade.guide.page.1.body:
The Trade Association buys and sells goods for U.M. (units of money).
1 U.M. is worth 1 emerald by default; an emerald block is worth 9 U.M.
Pay with money items and the change comes back in money items, largest first.
freetrade.guide.page.1.title: The Trade Association
freetrade.guide.page.2.body:
Price = b × (r ÷ x): b is the base value, r the reference stock and x the stock now.
Half the reference stock doubles the price.
Each trade moves the price a little (slippage), up to a ceiling.
Goods change hands in whole U.M. lots: 2 sticks may cost 1 U.M.
freetrade.guide.page.2.title: Prices and supply
freetrade.guide.page.3.body:
Items nobody declared get a value from the cheapest recipe that makes them.
Selling lots of logs lowers their price, so the planks and sticks made from them get cheaper too.
freetrade.guide.page.3.title: Values from recipes
freetrade.guide.page.4.body:
Give an unemployed villager an Auto Buyer as its workstation to make a Trade Representative.
Right-click it to open the trade window.
Sell one item type at a time from your inventory; the change comes back as money.
To buy, pick an item in the catalog and choose the amount.
freetrade.guide.page.4.title: The Trade Representative
freetrade.guide.page.5.body:
Set a ghost item to choose what it buys; drag one in from JEI or EMI.
A redstone signal makes it sell.
Adjacent chests and barrels multiply its capacity, up to 6x.
The money selector picks the money item for change. Hoppers take money out only with redstone.
freetrade.guide.page.5.title: Sell Point
freetrade.guide.page.6.body:
Put money in and it buys the item it is set to, at the catalog price.
Hoppers take items out only with a redstone signal.
freetrade.guide.page.6.title: Auto Buyer
freetrade.guide.page.7.body:
The association can charge a tax on sales and on purchases; the current rates are shown below. The tax goes to the server's OP account.
Buying back what you just sold costs more each time (backoff); the extra fades with time.
The treasury is the association's money: it pays for what players sell to it, and what players buy refills it. If the server uses a finite treasury and it runs empty, the association stops buying from players until someone buys from it. By default the treasury is infinite.
freetrade.guide.page.7.title: Taxes, backoff and treasury
freetrade.guide.title: Trade Association Guide
